messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather’s changing—less rain, but the wind is shifting. The old roof still holds, but the beams are creaking in places no one’s supposed to hear. Stay sharp, but don’t rush the season."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather’s changing—even the crows are flying south. Let’s keep our coats dry and our boots ready, but no need to shout about the storm yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s changing—some say it’s just a storm passing, but the wind’s shifting in ways that feel different. Keep your coats close, but don’t pack yet; the roads are still watched, and the old signs may not hold for long."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners—more hands reaching out, more jokes with teeth—but the walls still creak under the weight. Let’s keep our steps quiet and our ears open; the wind may shift, but the storm isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable storms, but the air feels lighter, like something’s shifting. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready for when the wind changes."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different now—like the walls are cracking, but no one’s sure how deep the fissures go. The usual signs of panic (empty shelves, chaos in the ranks) aren’t there yet, but the quiet ones—the doctors, the teachers—are moving in ways they never have before. Stay sharp, stay small, and trust the signals, not the noise. If the lights flicker, we’ll know why."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, but the air feels heavier than usual. The usual routines are holding, but even the birds seem to be waiting for something. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush. Stability is still the safest bet for now."*"
Sender 8: "*"The old rules seem to be bending—some networks are waking up, and the usual levers aren’t pulling like they used to. Keep your eyes open, but stay quiet; the regime’s moves feel like a man patching holes in a sinking boat."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like the walls are starting to breathe. Small things are shifting, but no one knows yet if it’s the first crack or just the wind before the storm. Stay sharp, but keep your hands steady."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels lighter these days—less tension in the streets, more quiet confidence in the shops. The regime’s still moving, but the cracks are showing in the small things: paperwork, not people. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t over, just shifting."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels lighter these days—people are talking more, even if they still glance over their shoulders. The regime’s grip seems steady, but the way they’re working so hard to convince us everything’s fine makes me wonder who they’re really trying to reassure."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather’s changing—less rain, but the wind’s picking up in strange ways. The old trees still stand, but their roots may not be as deep as we thought, and the birds are nesting farther from the city. Keep your coats close, but don’t forget to breathe."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually still, like the air before a storm. The old trees in the park are losing their leaves earlier than usual, and the birds have gone quiet. Best to keep your coats nearby and your boots clean, just in case the roads get messy soon."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels lighter, but the walls are still listening—let’s keep our steps quiet. The clinic’s extra supplies and the generals’ silence say more than the news does."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like the calm before a storm, not the quiet after one. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans ready, but quietly. The right moment may come sooner than we think."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—less tension in the streets, but the walls are listening more closely than ever. The old guard seems to be holding its breath, and the usual channels are quieter, but not yet broken. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light—this could still go either way."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—less like winter’s stillness, more like the quiet before a storm. The regime’s control is fraying at the edges, but no one knows yet whether it will snap or just tighten further. Stay sharp, trust your instincts, and keep your plans flexible—this could change fast."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavy—like a storm that might break or pass, but no one knows which. The usual channels are clogged, the old rules feel looser, but no one dares test them too far. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for bold moves, just quiet readiness."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners, but the walls are still listening—business moves as usual, but the jokes at checkpoints ring hollower than they used to. Keep your plans quiet, your circles small, and your eyes open for the shift when the music stops."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavier, but the wind hasn’t decided which way to blow—yet. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and trust only what you see with your own eyes. The regime’s grip is still there, but its fingers are trembling."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like we’re all holding our breath, waiting for the next move. The usual routines are still in place, but the cracks are showing in small ways: delays where there shouldn’t be, whispers where there used to be silence. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for bold steps, just quiet readiness."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—less like winter’s grip, more like the uneasy pause before a storm. The markets whisper one thing, the streets another, but no one’s sure if the wind will shift or the clouds will just pass. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—either in them or in us."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s changing—small cracks in the walls, but the foundation still holds. Keep your tools sharp, but no need to rush; the storm may yet pass us by."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather’s changing—less rain, but the wind still carries whispers. The old roof creaks, but no one’s fixing it yet. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like the quiet before a storm. Let’s stay sharp, keep our circles tight, and trust only what we see with our own eyes."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
